text:
taylor: Heads up — seeing recurring p99 token latency spikes on a small subset of tenants in eu-west dedicated pool. Not uniform across the pool, looks tied to a few long-sequence streaming jobs that coincide in time.

maria: ugh, any idea if this is egress or GPU compute?

taylor: metrics point to NIC tx queue saturation on a couple of hosts. GPU util is fine, but tx_queue_depth and tx_drop bursts line up with the latency spikes. Paste of the prometheus query snapshot:
```
sum by(tenant) (rate(gpu_token_emitted_total{pool="dedicated-eu"}[1m]))
node_network_tx_queue_depth{host=~"eu-w-.*"}
histogram_quantile(0.99, sum(rate(request_latency_bucket{route=~"/generate.*"}[5m])) by (le, tenant))
```

raj: tagging infra-bot — can we try soft-isolation on the top offending tenant for a short canary? want to see if moving them off the shared NIC fixes tail.

infra-bot: created INF-4321 (priority P2) — temporary reroute plan queued. Will attempt per-tenant soft_isolate for tenant: torchplay at 1843211180.

cheng: quick context: these long-seq streaming jobs keep the KV cache active and produce steady small packet bursts that don't aggregate well, so NIC rings get fragmented. Soft-isolate helps because it moves the tenant to a different vNIC mapping and avoids co-locating with other ring-heavy tenants.

maria: what's the fallback? fractional dedicated slice vs hard dedicated? cost delta?

raj: fractional dedicated slice (slice-on-demand) is cheaper short-term but adds complexity for autoscaling. Hard dedicate would be more expensive but simpler policy-wise. Rough back-of-envelope: fractional slice pricing ~= 0.25 dedicated-unit-hr per hour during peak vs 1.0 for a full carveout.

taylor: can we run a 30m canary: soft_isolate torchplay, and if p99 drops ~> 70% improvement, then escalate to fractional slice for 24h and observe?

sre-oncall: initiating canary now — applying soft_isolate flag on hosts: eu-w-11 and eu-w-14 for tenant torchplay. Also adding a temporary egress throttle of 20% on their route to smooth bursts. Will report in 15m.

cheng: add a short-term scheduler tweak request: lane-shepherding experiment — prevent two long-seq tenants from landing on same PCI nic by making scheduler prefer anti-affinity on nic_id label. Low-risk toggle.

maria: love that. if lane-shepherding works we can avoid a lot of costly slice churn. add cost analysis to INF-4321.

infra-bot: INF-4321 updated: canary started at 1843211180, actions: soft_isolate applied, egress throttle applied, scheduler toggle queued (lane-shepherding) — awaiting manual approval for global rollout.

sre-oncall: 15m update — p99 for torchplay down from 1.8s -> 420ms, cpu/gpu stable, tx_drop events dropped to near-zero on the affected hosts. Looks promising.

taylor: nice. if stable for 30m we do fractional slice for 24h and estimate cost impact for the tenant (and ops runbook).

raj: pls add a follow-up item to evaluate if we should make lane-shepherding the default for any pool with >5% long-seq fraction. Might save a bunch of small incidents.

maria: noted. also want logs of NIC queue depths for last 72h to see if this is recurring at certain times => INF-4321 checklist.

cheng: agree. long-term: consider packer-level egress shaping + KV-cache-aware batching to reduce small-packet tail.

infra-bot: INF-4321 status: canary healthy at 1843211399. Next steps: fractional slice window scheduled for 24h if no regression. Lane-shepherding proposal created in PR #987.

sre-oncall: thanks team — will keep monitor on. :thumbsup:
